model_interpretation.claim: The 4096-tile candidate was valid and faster in its reported three-run mean than the valid 2048-tile candidate; the measurements support testing a larger tile but do not prove it will improve performance further.
model_interpretation.applicability: The next tile-size test can compare against both measured two-pass candidates, but these results do not establish how performance scales beyond 4096 elements per CTA.
model_interpretation.next_experiment: Measure the 8192-tile program for correctness and repeated full-program timing, then compare with both candidates and the supplied baseline.

model_interpretation.claim: For large inputs, a 2048-element tile with 128-thread CTA reductions should produce far fewer partials than the baseline's repeated shrinking stages; a single CTA can finalize those partials in one second launch. This tests whether fewer stages outweigh the single-CTA finalizer's work, without assuming a speedup. Small inputs use a one-CTA path (or a direct operation for n=0/1) to avoid paying for a two-pass hierarchy.

model_interpretation.claim: Increasing the tile from 2048 to 4096 lets the single-CTA path cover inputs through 4096 and halves the partial count for larger inputs. This may reduce launch and finalization overhead, but the larger per-CTA workload and smaller first-pass grid could reduce parallel efficiency, especially for large inputs. The experiment tests that tradeoff against the valid 2048-tile parent; no speedup is assumed.

model_interpretation.claim: An 8192-element tile should halve the number of partials versus the measured 4096-element design and extend the single-CTA path to inputs up to 8192. For the largest supplied input, this means 512 partials instead of 1024; however, fewer first-pass CTAs may reduce parallel efficiency. This tests the tile-size tradeoff without assuming the larger tile is faster.

items.subject: Fewer launches with a two-pass hierarchy
items.objective: Using AB-MCTS, focus on the conventional multi-kernel hierarchy: vary tile/grain size and partial-count/finalization strategy to test lower-launch-count designs, including but not assuming a two-pass design wins. Avoid repeating a broad warp-reduction sweep already assigned to T1; use a straightforward correct CTA reduction unless tuning it is necessary to realize a hierarchy. Preserve exact arithmetic for all valid inputs, including safe intermediate sums, uninitialized scratch, tails, ABI, and default-stream behavior. If n=0 is valid, produce the empty sum. Report failures, correctness, and repeated full-program timings, then compare against the supplied baseline without treating one launch-count hypothesis as the result.
